title: Only Good Vibes, Part 2 – Looking at the Past and Future
content:
5. I’m still slow... Lots to study, lots to explore, lots of ideas. And I spend quite a large portion of the day sleeping—after the hospital, I mean. But I’m optimistic about the future!
5.1. The past 3 days I was off, and I had plans. Let me list them and talk about them (it was my vision of a perfect weekend):
5.1.1. Coding for the Shift project: I fixed some bugs, and right now I’m designing the templates.
5.1.2. I wanted to watch this movie called *Birdman* (2014), but I didn’t.
5.1.3. I did house chores and listened to *Sandman*. I didn’t find time to actually read, but the audiobook was fun too.
5.1.4. I wanted to study some easier chapters of OBGYN, but didn’t. In my defense, I went to the library twice and it was closed.
5.1.5. I did a lot of sleeping, cooking (god, my handmade food is good), and watched an enormous amount of sitcoms (mostly *How I Met Your Mother*).
5.1.6. I wanted to study French. I have a goal to do one or two 90-minute sessions of French on weekends, but sadly, I didn’t.

6. My goal is to make more time for the items in number 5—they really make me happy. It’s pretty damn late and I need to be up at 5 tomorrow, but I want to make a scheduled plan so I can find time for everything I think is cool!
7. All the plans and goals and living healthy are honestly a bit overwhelming, but also so exciting, and I can’t imagine my life any other way!

title: Only Good vibes Part 1
content:
Well, hello. It's August 25, 12:13 AM. I was meaning to share a post on recent events, but I was too lazy! Let me make bullet points and elaborate if needed.
1. I finally posted my notes on the war. Because of the internet block that week, I didn’t do it then. (It coincided with Star Wars, and I forgot to mention at the time—the only war I’m interested in is Star Wars!)
1.1. Of course, when you don’t know the war won’t actually last that long, it has a much grimmer face.
2. Reading my past notes tonight made me realize: I have a freakishly awesome life!
3. I’m an extern in OBGYN nowadays, my third ward after urology and neurology. I have to tell you this! I did my first intubation and CPR a month ago. The adrenaline rush was sooo good! I also took a Pap smear the other day. All in all, the hospital is fun, studying is fun, and life is fun!
4. I’m working on a new project called “Shift.” You can see it in my GitHub repositories!

title: Iran Israel War 2025 - Part 2, 11 AM - 12 PM
content:
I went home, depressed. I couldn’t even tell my family or boyfriend about yet another failure. I talked to my best friend though, Elaheh. And I did what I haven’t done since Iran’s protests in 2023—I scrolled and read and read all about how messed up everything has gotten. So many hours sitting in agony, real pain crumbling my body. The war has been going on for a couple of days, and I had managed to ignore the news to stay calm—a trick you learn in the Middle East. I tried to code or watch movies, but I was just too weak. At four I talked to my boyfriend. Then I got up to do some chores, water my beautiful plants. At 7 I opened my phone to look up summer makeups on Pinterest to try tonight and go out.
But war was crueler. The past weeks that I’ve been in Mashhad, I experienced pure joy. Walking in Vakil Abad Boulevard, seeing beautiful summer dresses and skirts, beautiful hairstyles, boys and girls hanging out in coffee shops. I remember braiding my hair, wearing my newly sewn skirt, and going to a bookshop with my boyfriend. He didn’t compliment my looks immediately, so I got upset. Seeing me like that, He told me to wait for him so he could go and buy me some sunflowers, and I said no. So stubborn...
I went walking so many nights in my sweet Vakil Abad, with Dana or Zahra and Mehran. Eating croissants, ice creams, matchas, and just walking and enjoying it all.
Back to today, I opened my phone and saw that my beloved city, Mashhad, had been under bombing attacks. Oh my sweet home. I cried when I recognized 17 Sharivar Street—a traditional bazaar and a couple of malls that are on that street.
As Freddie Mercury said, life still goes on.
I haven’t lost hope. I’m just extremely tired. I’m still hopeful—not for regimes to change, but for myself and for my loved ones. We will thrive somehow, someday, anyway.
I just wonder how it could’ve been in other circumstances.

title: Iran Israel War 2025 - Part 1, 6 AM - 4 PM
content:
Hey. It's the beginning of the summer of 2025. The weather is nice. I do not like talking about conflicts and politics, but I felt documenting it was necessary.
There have always been conflicts in the Middle East. I've known for a long time that I cannot change anything. I can only study, work hard, and get out.
That's where other heavy problems hit! The neurology attending won't let me pass my test. There has been a mistake—I can even verbally explain every question I answered. The med school won't even tell me what I did wrong. It's been 4 months since they put me on hold like this. They told me today they would give me my results and send me to class immediately. I got all ready this morning and went to the hospital by 7, just to hear that the attending wouldn’t even return the calls. It's 12 PM, and I have to try again and talk with the school tomorrow.
Life is so disappointing. You try, work hard, meditate, exercise, study, eat healthy—and in return, you are still struggling with depression.

title: Clear Head
content:
Hey, it's been two weeks since my last post, but it feels more like a month. Right now, the university (or more precisely, one of the attendings) is refusing to let me take my exam. I've been sitting outside the neurology ward at the hospital for hours, but that attending simply won't show up.
Our med school is a mess. Or maybe maltreating the juniors is a truth universally acknowledged.
On the bright side, I organized and cleaned my house, and fixed a few issues (with the help of my family and landlord). La famille came over last Thursday and left the day after.
I also did some coding for my Elrond project. I ran into trouble with Docker, mostly due to sanctions and internet filtering in Iran.
These days, I’m feeling a bit tired—fatigued, to be precise. I hit the gym 3 to 5 times a week, do yoga daily, try to eat healthy, and follow skin/hair care routines. Still, none of it really lifts my mood—at least not for long. They don't give me that "Yeah girl, you’re going to be as awesome and successful as you want to be" vibe. I wonder if I'm on the right path for myself.
All I know is, I should keep working and moving forward. Maybe I should watch House MD at a slower pace!
I don't know, I find comfort in immersing myself in stories.
I'm 5 pages away from finishing "The Old Man and the Sea", and I've loved it. I’ve been reading it in the hospital lobby while waiting for that attending. I might finish it tonight, but I also hope I find the strength to do some more coding.
Lately, I’ve had a few moments where I wondered, “What’s even the point?” I hope I can find a clear head, like the old man wished for.

title: Rainbows, Butterflies, and Grey Clouds
content:
Hey. It's Friday afternoon—May the Fourth—just kidding, it's actually May 9th. I went for a run this morning, visited a friend, and then stopped by a bakery to get some croissants.
Now it's 4:42 p.m. I have no idea where the day has gone. It's as if there’s a void, and I’ve been brainwashed into believing I actually spent the time doing something.
There’s a flower expo happening in Mashhad these days. I really wanted to go, but I’m just too tired.
Here’s a bullet-point list of what I’ve been up to lately—and what’s been bothering me.Finishing a post on a sad note is just too depressing, so I’ll start with the heavy stuff first.
Finishing my post with sad points, is just very depressing; So I start with them.
Cloud number 1: I’m still not an extern. What if I fall behind the bullies I see every day at university? They already hurt me all the time, and now I’m just giving them an excuse to mock me even more.
Cloud number 2:
I haven’t been as productive as I hoped. It’s been three months away from university—achievements? Hardly any. Well, let’s not be too harsh on myself, but I know I could’ve done better.
Cloud number 3: My legs hurt. I can’t bring myself to be productive today. I want to code—I know it makes me feel better—but right now, I just feel too burned out.
Okay, now let’s talk about the rainbows and butterflies.
R&B number 1: I pay for this school, so I’m not committed to working for the government for seven years. I’m going at my own pace, and it’s been pretty good, actually. Not perfect—but honestly, I don’t think I’m late for anything. I’m 23. How late can that be??
R&B number 2: Those bullies don’t have my coding skills, my ambition, or my goals. They’re just petit people.
R&B number 3: I’m eager to learn—and I enjoy it. That’s not something you can take away from me so easily.
R&B number 4: I try to stay healthy—physically and mentally—and I’m proud of that.
R&B number 5: I’ve made progress in Django and web development! I’m actually building something!
All in all, life isn’t bad. I’ve had better days, sure—but it’s fine. I’m ready to face the grey clouds a bit longer, hoping to see a rainbow soon.

title: Elrond 2.0
content:
Today, I'm gonna build Elrond project (one more time 😃) Here is what I want to build:
Elrond:Exchange Ideas and Discuss Issues
A specialized website for medical students and professionals.
Section 1: Exchange Ideas Users share: Articles, Research findings and Conference notes. Each user has a personal blog-style space. Other users can comment, discuss, and give feedback. And a tagging system for categorizing topics. Links to sources and references allowed.
Section 2: Discuss Issues Divided into: General Questions (e.g., study resources, exam techniques), Specialized Medical Questions (e.g., clinical cases), Community-driven answers. And upvote and ranking system highlights the best responses.
Further steps: Generative AI Integration: AI will learn from the growing Q&A database. Eventually offers automatic intelligent responses to questions. Improves speed, accuracy, and user experience. Becomes more helpful over time as data increases.

title: Reyhaneh's Descent into Despair
content:
Bonjour. It's 10:09 AM on a dull Wednesday, full of opportunities for me to do some work; or alternatively, let it all fall apart.
I made myself French toast and strawberry latte. The latte is sour, so I'm not a fan. I woke up, made breakfast, and browsed the social media.
Yesterday I went to Mashhads's university to ask when they'd send my grade to my university at Bojnurd. They said it will take at least ten more days. I'm falling behind far more than I expected. It's already been three months. You'd think I would’ve done something cool with all this free time; built a project, mastered a skill.
I thought that too.
But here I am, writing in a blog that I created a couple of weeks ago.
Maybe my only achievement.
But we know it's not enough, not even close.
Have you seen people who are referred to as "Effortless Beauty"?Well I've seen people who are effortlessly successful. I used to be like that; before medical school.
Now I'm just struggling.
I'm whatching a web development course. I hope I finish it soon. It's fun. You know, the other day I told one of those effortlessly successful people that I'm struggling to do the things that I like, and he said "Maybe you don't love it enough."Well, nowadays I'm just tired, and I do the things that I love; but with a heavy guilt. I'm no longer capable of enjoying anything fully. Maybe it's medical school's fault, I dream about it every night. Well, nightmares are dreams too, right?
Sandman hasn't been so nice to me lately.
Right now I'm going to do some house chores, watch that course and finish my pink latte. I'm not depressed or unmotivatad; I'm just losing hope. I try to ignore the guilt and keep my mood up(mostly by distracting myself). I hope the problems with medical school end soon.
Sorry for the messy writing, It’s hard to stay consistent when my thoughts aren’t.

title: Dead-end
content:
Hello. I created this blog to track my activities—just the things I do for fun.
"I’m going to play with physics," said Dr. Feynman,"…without worrying about any importance whatsoever. I’m just doing it for the fun of it."
For the past two months, I haven't attended medical school because I failed two subjects that, honestly, aren't all that important. But due to the rules, I have to wait to find another university to retake the exams.
At first, I thought, "Well, I can use this time to enhance my coding skills."
But I didn’t do much of that either.
I really believe this phase will pass, and I’ll get back on track—studying, coding, and learning French.
But over these last two months, I feel like I’ve accomplished nothing. What if I never make it? What if I never become as great as I dream? I didn’t try hard enough—neither for exams, nor for coding, nor for anything.
What if doing it for fun isn’t enough anymore? What if what it takes to be as great as my dreams isn’t just doing it for fun, but working way harder than I’ll ever be capable of? What if I can never stick to the plans?
Will I ever become the hardworking, focused person I need to be?
Stay tuned to this blog, and you'll see if I make it. :)
But for now, I feel very blue.
